config_delete_body: %1$s will be deleted from this device. This can't be undone.
config_details_missing: This configuration is no longer on this device.
config_done_body: Saved to this device only — always free.
config_duplicated: Copied. The duplicate is in your configurations.
config_export_body: Anyone who receives this link can use the server exactly as you do. Send it only to yourself or to somebody you would hand your password to.
config_export_warning: The export contains the keys that connect to the server.
config_invalid_conflicting: These parts of the link contradict each other: %1$s.
config_invalid_empty: There was nothing to read — the clipboard is empty.
config_invalid_encoding: Part of this link is encoded incorrectly, so Vazie VPN can't tell what it says.
config_invalid_malformed: This VLESS link isn't written the way one should be.
config_invalid_malformed_host: The server address isn't a hostname or an IP address.
config_invalid_malformed_user_id: The VLESS user ID isn't valid.
config_invalid_missing_parameter: This link is missing a parameter it needs: %1$s.
config_invalid_missing_reality_key: This REALITY configuration is missing its public key.
config_invalid_missing_user_id: The VLESS link has no user ID in it.
config_invalid_not_a_link: This doesn't look like a VLESS link.
config_invalid_other_scheme: Vazie VPN reads VLESS links; this one is %1$s.
config_invalid_port: The server port isn't a number between 1 and 65535.
config_method_example_a11y: An example of a configuration link
config_method_planned: For now Vazie VPN reads only %1$s, as one link or as a subscription. More formats are coming soon.
config_method_reads: Put your %1$s link or a subscription link in the field, or tap the button beside it to take it from the clipboard.
config_method_subscription: A subscription link works too: Vazie VPN opens it once to download its list of configurations. The request goes to that link's server and nowhere else.
config_method_unsure: Not sure what you have? Paste it anyway — if Vazie VPN doesn't recognise it, it will say so and won't try to guess.
config_paste_body: Tap Paste and Vazie VPN will read what is on your clipboard. It reads it here, on your device, and it goes nowhere else. A subscription link is the one exception: it is opened, to download its list.
config_rename_body: Only the name changes. The connection keeps working and nothing else about the configuration is touched.
config_review_kept_body: Vazie VPN doesn't recognise these parameters and saved them unchanged.
config_review_secrets_note: Keys and passwords stay hidden until you tap to reveal them, and never leave this device.
config_subscription_empty: There is nothing at this link that Vazie VPN can read as a configuration.
config_subscription_insecure: This subscription link starts with http. Vazie VPN downloads a subscription only over https, so nobody on the way can read it.
config_subscription_loading: Downloading the list of configurations from %1$s…
config_subscription_once: The list is downloaded once. If the subscription changes, add its link again.
config_subscription_refused: %1$s didn't give the list. The link may be mistyped or no longer valid.

config_subscription_skipped.one: %d more link was left out: Vazie VPN can't read it yet.
config_subscription_skipped.other: %d more links were left out: Vazie VPN can't read them yet.

config_subscription_too_large: What %1$s sent back is too large to be a list of configurations.

config_subscription_truncated.one: The list is longer. Vazie VPN adds the first %d at a time.
config_subscription_truncated.other: The list is longer. Vazie VPN adds the first %d at a time.

config_subscription_unreachable: Couldn't reach %1$s. Check your connection and try again.
config_unsupported_encryption: Vazie VPN understands this VLESS link, but VLESS encryption (%1$s) isn't supported yet.
config_unsupported_flow: Vazie VPN understands this VLESS link, but the %1$s flow isn't supported yet.
config_unsupported_security: Vazie VPN understands this VLESS link, but %1$s security isn't supported yet.
config_unsupported_transport: Vazie VPN understands this VLESS link, but the %1$s transport isn't supported yet.
connections_delete_body: %1$s will be removed from this device. If you have the original link you can import it again; if you do not, this cannot be undone.
connections_empty_body: Add a configuration from your VPN provider or your own server, and Vazie VPN will keep it here.
faq_unavailable: Couldn't load the questions. Check your connection and try again.

getting_started_first_config_intro: To use your own VPN, Vazie VPN needs a configuration — a link with the settings for a server. You usually get one from a VPN provider, from whoever runs the server, or from a server you run yourself.
getting_started_first_config_summary: What a configuration is and where to get one.
getting_started_manage_details_body: Open a configuration to rename it, duplicate it, or export it. Duplicating makes a second copy on this device; deleting removes it from this device only.
getting_started_manage_export_body: Export creates a shareable configuration. It can contain the credentials needed to connect, so treat it like a password.
getting_started_manage_intro: Once you have a configuration, everything you can do with it is in two places: the list, and the configuration's own screen.
getting_started_manage_list_body: Tap a configuration to use it. Swipe it to delete it — deleting always asks first.
getting_started_reads_body: %1$s. If Vazie VPN doesn't recognise a link, it will say so and won't try to guess.
getting_started_shape_body: It is normal for it to look like a long line of strange characters. Paste it into Vazie VPN and it will read the details for you.
guidance_appearance_body: The theme and the app icon: how Vazie VPN looks inside and on your home screen.
guidance_bug_body: Tell us in a short form: what happened and on which phone. Every report is read.
guidance_guides_body: Widgets, the Quick Settings tile, shortcuts and the notification — how to turn each on.
guidance_split_body: Choose apps that go around the VPN, or the only apps that go through it.
guidance_swipe_body: Swipe it to delete it. Everything else is in Details.
guide_notification_body_off: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can sit in your status bar with a Disconnect button on it — so you can stop it without opening the app. Notifications are off right now, so it can't.
guide_notification_body_on: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN sits in your status bar with a Disconnect button on it, so you can stop it without opening the app.
guide_notification_step_1: Open your phone's settings, then Apps.
guide_notification_step_2: Find Vazie VPN and open its notifications.
guide_notification_step_3: Turn on the VPN connection notification.
guide_notification_summary: The tunnel in your status bar, with a Disconnect button.
guide_quick_settings_body: Vazie VPN has a Quick Settings tile: one tap to open or close the tunnel, without opening the app.
guide_quick_settings_manual: How to add it by hand
guide_quick_settings_step_1: Pull the quick settings panel all the way down.
guide_quick_settings_step_3: Find Vazie VPN among the tiles that are not in use.
guide_quick_settings_step_4: Drag it up into the active tiles.
guide_quick_settings_summary: Open or close the tunnel without opening Vazie VPN.
guide_shortcuts_body: Holding the Vazie VPN icon offers your saved configurations directly. Nothing to set up — they are already there.
guide_shortcuts_step_1: Hold the Vazie VPN icon on your home screen.
guide_shortcuts_step_2: Let go on the configuration you want.
guide_shortcuts_summary: Hold the icon and pick one — nothing to set up.
guide_widgets_body: Two widgets: Quick Connect, which is one button, and a Dashboard with the session read-out. The button below asks your launcher for Quick Connect — add the Dashboard from the widget list.
guide_widgets_manual: How to add one by hand
guide_widgets_step_1: Hold an empty spot on your home screen.
guide_widgets_step_3: Find Vazie VPN. There are two.
guide_widgets_step_4: Choose a size and drag it out.
guide_widgets_step_5: For the Dashboard, find it in the same list and drag that one out too.
guide_widgets_summary: Quick Connect and a Dashboard, on your home screen.

notification_prompt_body: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can sit in your status bar with a Disconnect button on it — so you can stop it without opening the app. Vazie VPN connects either way.
onboarding_own_body: Vazie VPN ships with no servers, so the first thing to do is paste a VLESS link you already have. It is stored encrypted on this device and never uploaded — not to us, not to anyone. There is no account to create and nothing to pay for.
onboarding_reach_body: Two home-screen widgets, a Quick Settings tile in your pull-down panel, and your configurations under the app icon when you hold it. Nothing to set up right now — I'll point out the basics in a moment.
onboarding_reach_title: Vazie VPN without opening the app
onboarding_welcome_body: I look after the tunnel in this app. I'll be on the home screen telling you whether you're protected, and I'll be sleeping when you're not. Give me thirty seconds and I'll show you around.
onboarding_what_body: A VPN client: it opens an encrypted tunnel between this phone and a server, so the network you are on sees traffic to that server and nothing about where it goes next. Vazie VPN is the client. It is not a service that watches over you.
privacy_export_body: Export produces the original share link, and that link contains the credentials that connect to the server. Anyone who receives it can use the server as you. Vazie VPN hands it to Android's share sheet at the moment you ask and keeps no copy.
privacy_logs_body: Vazie VPN writes to the Android log only in debug builds, and never writes a key, a UUID, a share link or a server address into it. A release build is quiet.
privacy_never_account: No account, no email, no phone number, no device identifier: Vazie VPN never asks who you are.
privacy_never_analytics: No behaviour analytics, no advertising identifiers, no location. Vazie VPN sends no crash reports.
privacy_never_browsing: No browsing history, no visited addresses, no record of what you connected to or when, beyond the last-used timestamp above.
privacy_own_body: A configuration you imported is yours. It stays on this device, is never uploaded and costs nothing.
privacy_stores_choices: Your choices: which configuration is selected, the theme, the app icon, and which tips you have dismissed.
privacy_stores_configs: Your configurations: the server address, the port, the transport and security settings, and the keys needed to connect.
privacy_stores_usage: When each configuration was last used successfully — a timestamp, and nothing about what went through it.
privacy_surfaces_shortcuts: Long-pressing the icon offers up to three configurations by name. A name that looks like an address, a link, an e-mail, an IP or a UUID is left out rather than shortened: a launcher label is visible without unlocking anything.
privacy_surfaces_tile: The quick-settings tile shows the connection state and nothing else. It never names a configuration.
privacy_surfaces_widgets: A home-screen widget shows the selected configuration's name, its protocol and the session's duration and traffic. Those are stored in the widget's own preferences so it can draw itself while Vazie VPN is closed — on this device, and never a key or an address.
privacy_vpn_body: While connected, your traffic goes through the server in the configuration you chose. That server can see the destinations your device asks for, exactly as your network provider could otherwise. Vazie VPN is the client; it does not run in between.
privacy_vpn_dns: DNS queries follow the tunnel while it is up, so they go to the same server rather than to your provider.
privacy_where_backup: Nothing is included in Android's cloud backup. A restored phone starts with no configurations rather than with keys that travelled through somebody else's storage.
privacy_where_encrypted: Configurations and their keys are encrypted on this device, with a key held by Android's keystore. They are not readable by other apps and are not copied anywhere.
privacy_where_plain: Your theme, icon and dismissed tips are in a plain file — they are preferences, not secrets, and keeping them out of the encrypted store means a display setting cannot break the store that holds your keys.
settings_app_icon_body: Changes the icon on your home screen. Your configurations and any live connection are untouched; some launchers take a moment to catch up.
settings_app_icon_themed_hint: If your phone recolours icons to match its theme (themed icons), Monochrome or Pearl on the Light background will look best.
settings_boosty_body: Vazie VPN is made by one person, in the evenings and at weekends. Helping is entirely optional and unlocks nothing — there is nothing to unlock. The app is free and always will be.
